chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj, from Sulayman ibn Khalid who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Verily, God, Mighty and Majestic, says:
"And that to your Lord is the ending" (53:42)
So when speech (discussion) reaches God (His Essence), hold back (and stop there).

key_terms.الْكَلَام: Speech or theological discourse — here referring to theological speculation about God's nature
key_terms.الْمُنْتَهَى: The ultimate end/termination point — God's Essence as the absolute boundary of rational inquiry
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic — an honorific for God emphasizing His transcendence
key_terms.فَأَمْسِكُوا: Hold back/stop — a command to cease theological speculation when it reaches God's Essence

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the limits of theological speculation about God?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) invokes Quran 53:42 to establish the theological principle that rational inquiry about God's nature must have a limit. The verse 'and that to your Lord is the ultimate end' signifies that God's Essence is the absolute termination point beyond which human speech and speculation cannot legitimately go. This hadith is part of the chapter on the forbiddance of discussing the 'how' (kayfiyya) of God, reflecting the Shia theological position that affirms God's attributes while prohibiting anthropomorphic speculation.
